claims.head: A shadow job for Teräväinen, Frondell and Mangiapane
claims.call: The Blackhawks’ L3 (Teräväinen, Frondell and Mangiapane) spends at least 46% of its 5-on-5 time against the Sabres’ first line, against about 35% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Blackhawks keep sending Frondell’s line (Teräväinen, Frondell and Mangiapane) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jeff Blashill has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Sabres’ first line is Benson, Krebs and Thompson.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 39%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Konsta Helenius is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 4 games.
Zach Metsa has started killing penalties: on the ice for 36% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, up from 7% last season.
Josh Norris has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 16 games, up from 1% last season.
Patrick Kane is out (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward. Tyler Bertuzzi has taken his spot beside Connor Bedard and Roman Kantserov.

Bowen Byram is on injured reserve and has missed the last 10 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Wyatt Kaiser has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov. That pair has had 32% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 109:51 together, down from 47% with Byram.
Dillon Boucher was added to the roster on Nov 4 and has played beside Cole Smith and Ryan Greene.

story.head: The Blackhawks are searching for answers
paras: The Sabres won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-3 in Buffalo on Oct 3. The Blackhawks are winless in five (0-4-1), while the Sabres (8-5-3) beat Columbus 5-2 on Friday. The Sabres played last night, and the Blackhawks are rested. Going in, the Sabres are sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 14th in the NHL) and the Blackhawks last in the Central (31st).

The Sabres’ record (.594) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.540), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. The Blackhawks haven’t played well, but their record (.265) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .379, and their finishing has held them back.
In their five-game skid, the Blackhawks have been outscored 23-11, including 14-8 at 5-on-5.

The Blackhawks (32nd) and the Sabres (30th) both don't block many shots. The Sabres rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd) and get their shots through to the net (4th). As for the Hawks, they do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest) and have struggled on the power play (32nd). Chicago has scored 2.18 goals a game, the second fewest in the league, and allowed 3.94, the second most.

Tage Thompson (10 G / 9 A / 19 P in 16 GP) leads the Sabres in scoring, with ten points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against Chicago. Jack Quinn (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 16 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Blackhawks, Connor Bedard (4 G / 8 A / 12 P in 11 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Roman Kantserov (8 G / 2 A / 10 P in 17 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (5-3-3 / .878 SV% in 10 GS) will likely start for Buffalo, and Spencer Knight (4-9-0 / .891 SV% in 13 GS) for Chicago.

At home, Jeff Blashill likes to send Teräväinen, Frondell and Mangiapane out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Benson, Krebs and Thompson. One more thing: the Sabres usually control more of the chances than the Blackhawks do.
